title: Why your product needs an AI product manager, and why it should be you — James Lowe, i.AI
talk_summary: A UK government AI incubator lead argues that AI product management is a distinct discipline requiring AI expertise, illustrated with three products (Consult/ThemeFinder, Minute, Redbox). The transferable mechanisms are: validate AI capability with evals before building product, go wide on features then strip back, and pivot fast when the landscape changes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of building the product around existing NLP techniques, they got real-user data plus synthetic data, built evals, optimized against them, then tested outputs with real users before committing to a product shape.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We got data from real users and generated synthetic data to create eval which we optimized against.
takeaways.numbers: Output comparable to humans, 1000x faster and 400x cheaper

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately built many experimental features for different user groups, tested with real users, then cut everything that didn't work, aided by low sentimental attachment to AI-generated code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Experiment hard and go wide with lots of features... but then cut back and and streamline the app down.

takeaways.what_they_do: Prioritizing the AI capability first revealed exactly where human input added value in the pipeline, which changed the product design.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by prioritizing the AI capability, what we found was the key points in the package in the pipeline where human input and human in the loop was really valuable

takeaways.what_they_do: When a free enterprise chat product appeared and MCP standardized tool/data access, they stopped betting on their own client being the only interface and invested in MCP instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It no longer made sense for us to bank on red box being the main way... we've been investing hard in using the model context protocol
